description: Early-development baseline bead-rs binary, built before the attempt-resolution work began. Metadata was reconstructed from the binary's own embedded version string during the beadrs-b6441e82 re-verification, because no staging metadata was recorded when this binary was pinned.
git_commit_message: chore(beadrs-4fcead71): release 0.2.4 — v0.2.3 tag landed behind a checkpoint commit
build_features: default (the attempt-resolution feature does not exist in the 0.2.4 tree)
notes: Commit attribution comes from the binary's embedded version string (`bead-pre-feature --version`), which build.rs derives from git at compile time. docs/pinned-binaries.md previously attributed this binary to 181f181; that is wrong — 181f181 is 31 commits later and its Cargo.toml declares 0.2.6, while the pinned binary embeds 0.2.4/af023ad. The docs have been corrected.

Because the attempt-resolution cargo feature does not exist at this commit, this binary is a true pre-feature baseline: any hash difference against the bead-attempt-resolution-* pins reflects all intervening development, not the feature flag (which is an empty marker feature that gates no code).

sha256 is NOT reproducible across rebuilds: build.rs re-embeds BEAD_BUILD_TIMESTAMP whenever .git/index changes, so a rebuild of identical source hashes differently. Verify by hash comparison against this file; never by rebuilding.
restored_lineage_note: git_commit_sha above is built-from provenance: it names a commit of the force-pushed-away lineage that no longer exists in any clone (verified 2026-09-03). restored_lineage_twin_sha is its content twin (same subject, author date, tree content) and is the rebuild target via scripts/build-from-archive.sh. The recorded binary_sha256 is hash-only, not rebuild-verifiable, until SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH determinism lands (beadrs-dc295092 / beadrs-baba38b8). Re-pinned by beadrs-e030cc56, 2026-09-03. Twin re-verified 2026-09-03 by beadrs-ed36ef53 (close-out doc reconciliation): twin commit resolves with the recorded subject, git_commit_sha is confirmed unresolvable here, and binary_sha256 matches the pinned bytes on disk.
